items.text: In Deep Mud
Mental Health Consultation Room, Laplace

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Welcome, Ms. Klara.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: I'm your attending psychiatrist.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Before we start the session, I'd like to confirm something.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: What happened to make you lose control of your arcane skill?

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Do you remember?
Memories flash before her, jumbled and messy.
She closes her eyes as she tries to recall.
She's taken back to her days in Vienna.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Zemfira, I ...

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: This is as far as you go, my friend.

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: We've walked a long way. You should head home. It's best not to be alone in the dark.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What about you?

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: We enter the world alone, and we leave it alone. It's the natural way of things.

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: Don't worry, my dear Kakania. We'll see each other again.

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: I promise.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But Russia is so very far away. Are you sure you'll still remember this place?

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: I will remember.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: May I at least walk you to the edge of town? There's a station there. I can take the tram back.

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: No need.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I want to remember our last day together. Is it so awful to want to extend it just a little longer?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Or is it because you don't want to see me anymore? If that's the case, I'll return the hand mirror you gave me right now.

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: It's because everything I wanted to say has been said. And the blessing has taken effect.

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: Simply looking at you makes me happy. It gives me hope to know there are still good people like you in the world.

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: That's why I gave you my blessing. As long as you don't break the mirror, you will feel its effects.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What are you talking about?! Of course I won't break it!

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: Then please don't ever say that you'll give it back. And remember these words:

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: "Disaster will fall on the shards of a broken mirror."

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: Don't forget.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I won't. Although I still don't understand.

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: Ask no more, dear Klara.

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: You kept asking us wanderers what we wanted. You learned that Illich desires fortune and that Laurel longs for a life free from hiding.

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: But I haven't given you my answer yet.

items.speaker: Zemfira
items.text: What I'm looking for is ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What do you long for, Zemfira?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And where is the mirror you gave me?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: My mirror, the hand mirror.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It appears ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It appears that every time I think of it, either my memory or my arcane skill goes wrong.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: I see. There's a close connection between your symptoms and your hand mirror. Noted.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Then, let's take a deeper dive into your mirror.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Could you describe it to me?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Hmm.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It's ornate. Finely decorated.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But it's far more than an ornament. It's my very first hand mirror.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And it shall never be broken.
Living Room, the Vingler House

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Elbert!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Look! My first hand mirror! My friend and I had a discussion, and I've decided to use it as a key element to improving my self-awareness.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Klara! You're back!

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: A hand mirror? May I have a look?

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Such a delicate mirror! It is perfect for your first hand mirror.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: "Your first hand mirror is for reflecting yourself. Your first table mirror is for observing others." The only thing missing is the Vingler family crest. You'd better present it to Father for his approval.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Why should I? I have no need for his approval!

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Please consider it for me, would you, Klara?

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: Father would so like to know about this. He's always wanted to understand you better.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Fine! If I must, I'll show him the mirror. But I don't want his approval or the crest.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'll simply present it to him. I won't allow him to destroy it.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: *sigh* You can't keep doing this.

items.speaker: Elbert
items.text: You really should ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I already know what he's going to say.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "You really should show more respect for Father."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "You really should be more restrained. Don't disgrace yourself."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "Stop associating with the lower class."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "Act like a decent middle-class lady."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "And become a part of this 'beautiful society.'"

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Should I really?

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Ms. Klara?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm sorry. What are you talking about?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Oh, my mind wandered again? Sorry.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: No worries. It happens.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: You were talking about the hand mirror and your brother, Elbert.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Is there anything else you want to share with me?
Is there? She asks herself.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I don't recall where the hand mirror ended up. Perhaps it's broken.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: People say that a broken mirror is a bad omen.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: You've mentioned that it carries some kind of "blessing," though it sounds more like a prophecy to me.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: A prophecy, yes, of the disaster that would follow the breaking of the mirror.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And it has come true.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Because of that "blessing," Vienna is gone, and Elbert lost his arm.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: All because of that broken hand mirror.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Like the one that broke in the "Storm"?

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Actually, we don't know where the hand mirror is, and "prophecy" is just my personal understanding of it, not an objective truth.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: So let's not jump to conclu—
Kakania jumps to her feet.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You're right. It IS a prophecy. The mirror must be broken!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: That's why I can't do anything! It's because my mirrors are broken.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: All of them.
At the moment she buries her head in her arms, the mirrors in the room start to tremble.
They shake and crack, one after another, as Kakania falls back into her memories yet again.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Ah!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: It's breathtakingly exquisite.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: It looks more like a frame for a delicate piece of art than a mirror.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: And look at the spider web detailing. Just gorgeous.

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: What is this thing?

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: It's pure blasphemy!

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: This is hardly a mirror, let alone one to be associated with the Vingler name! It's an utter disgrace!

items.speaker: Middle-Aged Male
items.text: Klara Vingler! What do you think you're doing?!
Her memories swirl in her mind, surrounding her like the fragments of broken glass that are now all over the floor. She sits with her head in her arms, her body shivering.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Yes, the mirror is broken, just like ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Vienna is broken.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What on earth can I do?
